newsitem.title: USA: Incoming Citadel head says no coverup in hazing.
newsitem.headline: Incoming Citadel head says no coverup in hazing.

text.p: The president-elect of The Citadel Monday expressed support for the disciplinary action taken against 10 cadets accused of hazing two of the four women enrolled in the formerly all-male military college.
"All violations have been identified, no action has been covered up, overlooked or missed," General John Grinalds said in his first news conference since being selected to lead the college.
The school's administration dismissed one student and disciplined nine others because of the allegations by former cadets Jeanie Mentavlos and Kim Messer.

The women claimed their clothes were set on fire and that they were forced to drink tea until they vomited. They also said they were called degrading names, hit with the butt of a rifle and made to stand in a closet for long periods of time.
The four women enrolled last fall after the school dropped its all-male admission policy when the U.S. Supreme Court ruled a similar policy at Virginia Military Institute was unconstitutional.
Messer and Mentavlos completed the fall semester but did not return to school following the Christmas break.

Grinalds will take over as president of the 154-year-old state-supported school in July. He said he was dedicated to assimilating women into the cadet corps but declined to share his views on how to do so, saying he wanted to wait until he was installed and "takes a look around."

The U.S. Justice Department and the State Law Enforcement Division of South Carolina were conducting separate investigations into the hazing. Grinalds said he had "no idea of what their conclusion would be."

Grinalds spent the past four days on campus taking part in events surrounding Corps Day, which commemorates the college's founding. He said he met with students and faculty members and was surprised to find them upbeat.
"I expected a siege mentality," he said. Instead he said he found students with a commitment to the mission that The Citadel is a "special place" that will train "educated, principled" leaders.
Grinalds is the headmaster of Woodberry Forest School, a boy's preparatory school in Virginia. He served for 32 years in the U.S. Marines and is a graduate of West Point.
